developments.name: Haskalah (Jewish Enlightenment)
ideals: Integration into European society ('Be a Jew at home and a man in the street')

developments.name: Emancipation and Modern Denominational Splintering
outcomes: Granting of citizenship to Jews across Western Europe
Emergence of Reform Judaism in Germany (Abraham Geiger, Samuel Holdheim)
Counter-reaction of Neo-Orthodoxy (Rabbi Samson Raphael Hirsch: Torah im Derekh Eretz)

developments.name: The Shoah (Holocaust)
developments.event: Systematic, industrialized genocide orchestrated by Nazi Germany murdering 6 million Jews (two-thirds of European Jewry)
developments.theological_impact: Post-Holocaust Jewish theology (Emil Fackenheim's 614th Commandment not to give Hitler posthumous victories; Richard Rubenstein; Elie Wiesel; Rabbi Joseph B. Soloveitchik Kol Dodi Dofek)

developments.name: Zionism and the Re-establishment of the State of Israel
principles: Modern political Zionism founded by Theodor Herzl (1897 First Zionist Congress in Basel)
Proclamation of the State of Israel on 14 May 1948 (5 Iyar 5708)
Crucial Distinction: Political Zionism as a modern national-liberation movement vs the eternal religious-covenantal yearning for Zion (Epistemic Rule 1.5)
